title: Frontend Developer Roadmap
summary: A practical path for learners who want to build polished user interfaces, understand browser fundamentals, and prepare strong portfolio projects for internships.
audience: Best for juniors who enjoy visual building, interaction design, and turning ideas into usable screens.

sections.title: Frontend Foundations
sections.description: Build strong browser, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fundamentals before rushing into frameworks.

items.title: Master semantic HTML and responsive CSS layouts
items.description: Learn how to structure pages clearly, use semantic tags, and build layouts that adapt well across mobile and desktop screens.
items.whyItMatters: A lot of junior frontend problems come from weak layout and structure skills, not from missing frameworks.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build clean landing pages, forms, and dashboards without copying layout code blindly.

miniProjects.title: Student Club Landing Page
miniProjects.summary: Create a responsive landing page for a university coding club with sections, call-to-action areas, and a contact form.

commonMistakes.title: Using generic divs for everything
commonMistakes.explanation: This makes pages harder to read, maintain, and navigate with assistive technology.

commonMistakes.title: Designing only for desktop first
commonMistakes.explanation: Internship reviewers often check how your pages behave on smaller screens and uneven content lengths.

items.title: Learn JavaScript fundamentals and DOM interaction
items.description: Get comfortable with variables, functions, arrays, objects, async basics, and connecting JavaScript logic to UI behavior.
items.whyItMatters: Without core JavaScript understanding, React often feels like memorizing patterns instead of solving problems.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build interactive components like tabs, filters, and form validation without depending on a framework.

miniProjects.title: Simple Budget Tracker UI
miniProjects.summary: Create a small budgeting interface where users can add and remove expenses and see totals update in real time.

commonMistakes.title: Trying to memorize syntax without building
commonMistakes.explanation: You retain JavaScript faster when each concept is tied to a visible interaction.

commonMistakes.title: Avoiding debugging tools
commonMistakes.explanation: Console logging and browser devtools are part of the skill, not a sign of weakness.

sections.title: Framework and Application Skills
sections.description: Move from isolated UI exercises to structured applications using React and modern frontend workflows.

items.title: Build with React using component thinking
items.description: Learn props, state, conditional rendering, forms, lists, and reusable component patterns.
items.whyItMatters: Most frontend internships expect you to work with a component-based mindset, not just static pages.
items.expectedOutcome: You can turn a UI into reusable components and explain your state decisions clearly.

miniProjects.title: Study Planner App
miniProjects.summary: Build a study planner where users can add learning tasks, filter by priority, and track completion.

commonMistakes.title: Putting too much logic in one component
commonMistakes.explanation: Large components become hard to debug and make future features slower to add.

commonMistakes.title: Using state for everything
commonMistakes.explanation: Some values can be derived directly and do not need separate state variables.

items.title: Use Next.js for routing, layouts, and data-driven pages
items.description: Learn file-based routing, shared layouts, basic server rendering, and how data flows into pages.
items.whyItMatters: Next.js is a practical stack skill for internships and gives structure to portfolio apps.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build a multi-page app with shared layout, navigation, and data-backed sections.

miniProjects.title: Internship Board UI
miniProjects.summary: Create a small internship listings app with category pages, a detail page, and a saved-items interaction.

commonMistakes.title: Making every component client-side by default
commonMistakes.explanation: That removes some of the performance and simplicity benefits that App Router gives you.

commonMistakes.title: Letting routes and components grow without structure
commonMistakes.explanation: A clean route and component structure makes projects easier to explain in interviews.

sections.title: Portfolio and Job-Ready Delivery
sections.description: Strengthen the practical skills that help your work look ready for internship review.

items.title: Ship portfolio projects with polish and clarity
items.description: Improve one or two portfolio projects so they feel complete, understandable, and worth reviewing.
items.whyItMatters: A smaller number of well-finished projects is usually more convincing than many unfinished ones.
items.expectedOutcome: You can present a frontend project with clear structure, good README documentation, and strong UX details.

miniProjects.title: Portfolio Case Study Upgrade
miniProjects.summary: Take an existing project and improve onboarding, edge cases, empty states, and README explanation.
stretchGoals: Write a short design tradeoff note

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring loading, empty, and error states
commonMistakes.explanation: Reviewers notice when an app only works in the happy path.

commonMistakes.title: Treating the README like an afterthought
commonMistakes.explanation: A strong README helps recruiters and mentors understand your thinking quickly.

items.title: Work with APIs, version control, and team-friendly habits
items.description: Practice integrating APIs, organizing commits, and communicating how features are built.
items.whyItMatters: Internships often measure whether you can collaborate and reason about work, not only whether the UI looks nice.
items.expectedOutcome: You can connect a frontend app to an API, explain your implementation, and keep your project history understandable.

miniProjects.title: Career Dashboard Integration
miniProjects.summary: Connect a frontend dashboard to mock roadmap and jobs data, then document your implementation choices.

commonMistakes.title: Using fetch logic you do not really understand
commonMistakes.explanation: It becomes hard to debug when data shape, loading states, or failures change.

commonMistakes.title: Committing large unrelated changes together
commonMistakes.explanation: Cleaner commit history makes it easier to review your thinking and recover from mistakes.
